
## What Is a Record Class? (Java 16+)

A **record** is a special class used to create **immutable data objects** with **very less boilerplate code**.
🔹 Without Record (Old Way)
```java
public class Employee {
    private final int id;
    private final String name;

    public Employee(int id, String name) {
        this.id = id;
        this.name = name;
    }

    public int getId() { return id; }
    public String getName() { return name; }
}
```

✅ With Record (Java 16+)
```java
public record Employee(int id, String name) {
}
```

### ✅ Automatically Generated by Record:

-   Constructor
-   Getters (`id()`, `name()`)
-   `equals()`
-   `hashCode()`
-   `toString()`
-   Immutable fields

✅ Usage Example
```java
public class Test {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        Employee emp = new Employee(101, "Vamshi");
        System.out.println(emp.id());
        System.out.println(emp.name());
    }
}
```
### ✅ When to Use Record

-   DTOs
-   API request/response models
-   Immutable data holders
-   Kafka messages, REST DTOs
